lines.en: I remember the first time I read a novel.
The texture of soft paper against my fingertips.
Black letters blooming across a vast white expanse.
The feel of the pages as I folded them over and turned them with my own hands.
「Reading the letters isn't what matters. What matters lies between the lines.」
My mother, who loved books, would sometimes say that. But to my younger self, at least, it wasn't a metaphor.
The gaps between one letter and the next.
My own little snowfield (雪原), sitting all alone between them.
That space, absurdly narrow for anyone to enter and lie down in, was just right for a child like me who loved to hide.
Rustle, rustle.
With each pleasant sound, the letters piled up like snow.
Within them, I became the protagonist, went on adventures, fell in love, and dreamed.
And so I read, and read, and read again.
The moment a story that had seemed as though it would never end came to an end, and I closed a book for the first time.
Even now, I remember that feeling, as though I had been cast out of the world.

The feeling of the protagonist and supporting characters walking into the sentence ‘And they lived happily ever after,’ leaving me alone beyond the story's final period. Amid the emptiness and sense of betrayal, my younger self struggled, unable to bear the loneliness.
「Is this······ ‘the end’?」
Perhaps it was something like learning about death.
Realizing for the first time that something was finite.
My mother said,
「That is ‘the end.’」
「Isn't there anything after this?」
「There's nothing after it.」
My mother was cold, as though stating a cruel truth about life.
「But just because you've seen ‘the end’ doesn't mean you've seen the whole story.」
And wise.
「What?」
「Read it again.」
Reading a finished story again.
As a child, I couldn't see what meaning there could be in that.
「Why would I read a story again when I already know all of it?」
「If you read it again, it will surely become a different story.」
「······I don't want to.」
Afraid of feeling that loss again, I stubbornly refused.
Then my mother said,
「Shall we read it together, then?」
That was how I learned to ‘reread.’
Where I had seen only the protagonist's perspective the first time, I saw the supporting characters' perspective the second time, and the enemy's perspective the third.
A story that changed each time I read it.
The story had ended, yet it wasn't over.
As long as the reader doesn't give up on a story, the story doesn't end.
Even now, I sometimes wonder.
What if my mother had told me something different then?
That novels were all make-believe, and reading them only wasted your life.
Would I have made lots of friends?
Would I have studied hard, avoided being ostracized, and stayed instead of running from the reality I had been given?
Bzzzzzt!
Sparks flared in the air, shattering the stream of memories.
「Kim Dokja. You seem to have time on your hands.」
When I turned my head, someone was standing in the pitch-black darkness.
A being who could easily enter someone else's dreams.
Unless they were a mighty divine being, only a prophet could do such a thing.
But this wasn't Anna Croft.
「Are you finding your ‘fate’ bearable?」
It was a face I knew.
A wanderer wearing old clothes and a battered crown.
Come to think of it, there were ‘prophets’ among the constellations, too.
‘The One Who Stabbed His Own Eyes.’
He was ‘King Oedipus’ of <Olympus>, whom I had met at the banquet.
King Oedipus said to me,
「Fate is approaching.」
‘Fate? Shouldn't that already have been fulfilled? I died, just as you planned, didn't I?’
「This is not a fate you can evade with some paltry Story. Soon, you must decide whose side you will take. I believe you will make the right choice.」
‘I'm not taking anyone's side.’
Then King Oedipus smiled.
「You will come to <Olympus> without fail. Of all the incarnations I have seen, none has had a story so well suited to <Olympus> as yours.」
‘What bullshit······.’
Bzzzzt!
Before I could finish, the memories came flooding in again.
「Dokja.」
Damn it.
This memory again.
The bloodstained living room.
Mom stood before a dead man's body, holding a knife.
「From now on, you're going to read all of this ‘again.’」
Mom smiled and spoke to me as I trembled all over.
「So you must remember it well. All right?」
A nightmare crashing into me head-on.
I let out a scream that couldn't be heard.
King Oedipus's voice rang out as though mocking every one of those memories.
「Inherit <Carnival of Lightning>. Otherwise, in the next scenario, you will die ‘forever.’」
[The perk of the attribute ‘Eight Lives’ activates.]
[Your body is resurrected!]
A choking gasp burst out, as though I were coughing up amniotic fluid.
[The snake's second head is sacrificed.]
[This head's ability is ‘Intelligence (知能).’]
Warmth returns to my cold skin, and my slack muscles regain their strength.
This already makes the fourth time I've experienced death.
Once while killing the fire dragon, once during the Disaster of Floods, once while facing Nirvana······ At this point, I had to wonder whether Yoo Joonghyuk was the sunfish or I was.
“······Ugh, where am I this time?”
I looked around, but I couldn't work out where I was.
All I could see was ground as soft and billowy as white clouds, and an open sky.
······Had there been a place like this in the [Dark Castle]?
[The perk's effect increases your thinking speed.]
Perhaps thanks to the resurrection perk, my grasp of the situation was quicker and clearer.
For now, I decided to retrace everything from the beginning, one step at a time.
First, the biggest question.
‘Why did I die?’
I had definitely left my body in Han Sooyoung's care while using the third-person viewpoint on <Paradise>.
Then my consciousness had suddenly faded, and a death message had appeared.
In other words, there was only one possible conclusion.
Someone had killed me while I was asleep.
······But who the hell was it? Han Sooyoung?
[A new achievement is recorded in your fifth Story.]
[People will remember you as the ‘Messiah Who Knows Shame.’]
Because I'd happened to die at such a strange moment, a strange achievement had been added to my Story, too.
······Surely I hadn't actually died of embarrassment.
Since the prophecy was that ‘Incarnation Kim Dokja would be killed by someone he loved,’ whoever killed me would at least be ‘someone I loved.’
“Hey, Kim Dokja! You're alive again?”
Just then, Han Sooyoung was sauntering toward me from afar.
“What happened?”
“We were attacked.”
Han Sooyoung grumbled as she gazed across the empty cloud plain.
A place where, no matter where you looked, there was nothing but drifting clouds.
The scene was far too peaceful for the word ‘attack.’

“As soon as you fell asleep, these guys suddenly appeared and came after you. I did my best to stop them, but it didn't go well. Somehow you ended up fatally wounded, and I ran like hell with you, crying and wailing, and suddenly we were in a place like this.”
Her explanation flowed as naturally as the clouds, but it was utterly unbelievable.
[The exclusive skill, ‘Lie Detection Lv.2,’ activates!]
[You have confirmed that the statement is true.]
“······Did you see the attackers' faces?”
“They were all masked, so I couldn't get a good look. I checked a few of them with [Detect Attributes], but they were people I didn't really know.”
Han Sooyoung had grown considerably stronger during our three-day journey in search of hidden pieces.
At her current level, Han Sooyoung would rank around 20th in the Dark Castle at the very least.
Yet these people were skilled enough to get past her protection, kill me, and even imprison us here.
No matter how much I thought about it, I couldn't think of any group that fit.
“Didn't you find out anything else?”
“You've been pretty damn full of yourself this whole time, haven't you? Someone's been working herself to death for three days······.”
“Three days?”
“You've been dead for three days. Didn't you know?”
Come to think of it, I'd forgotten that the ‘Eight Lives’ attribute required a waiting period.
Three days······ Damn it.
What had happened to the others?
Surely they hadn't already moved on to the next scenario.
If they had, all my plans would go awry.
Han Sooyoung sighed and said,
“No matter how far I wander, there's nothing but clouds around here. I've already given up.”
“······Is that why you've let your clones out to do that?”
Throughout the clouds, Han Sooyoung's clones were each practicing different skills.

A Han Sooyoung practicing [Hidden Weapons], a Han Sooyoung practicing [Footwork], a Han Sooyoung training in [Hand-to-Hand Combat]······ Every Han Sooyoung was absorbed in improving her own skill proficiency.
“It's my own training method. I didn't want to waste all that time waiting for you······ If I do that and then retrieve the clones, my skill proficiency goes up faster.”
Somehow, I felt I understood a little of the secret behind how Han Sooyoung had grown so strong in such a short time.
“What is this, Na■to?”
“You mean Naru■? Damn······ Even stuff like that gets filtered here. Well, I did get the idea from it.”
Just what you'd expect from a plagiarist. Honestly.
Suddenly, I find myself curious.
Even the original ‘Ways of Survival’ doesn't explain the [Avatar] skill in much detail. It wouldn't hurt to learn a bit about it while I had the chance.
“Doesn't that skill have any restrictions? Can you make an unlimited number of clones as long as you have enough magic power?”
“That would be overpowered. Of course it has restrictions. Every time I use the skill, I have to give the avatar some of my memories.”
“······Some of your memories? What if the avatar dies?”
“Then I lose those memories, too.”
Watching Han Sooyoung answer so casually, I felt a little unnerved.
Wasn't this a skill that could give you Alzheimer's if something went wrong?
As though she'd read my thoughts, Han Sooyoung gave a little laugh and said,
“Don't worry. I usually make them with memories I don't need. And as long as I retrieve them properly, the memories come back intact. Sometimes······ one gets out of my control, which is a problem.”
“Out of your control?”
“There's a clone I made the first time I used [Avatar]······ Maybe I gave it too many memories, because it suddenly became uncontrollable and I couldn't retrieve it.”
“······That can happen? Then what about the memories it had?”
Han Sooyoung shrugged.
“Who knows? But since I'm fine now, they probably weren't anything important.”
“So you think you're fine.”
“Shut up.”
Was it just my imagination that made me feel that clone might have important memories?
The thought that a clone who looked exactly like Han Sooyoung might still be wandering somewhere in Seoul sent a strange chill down my spine.
One by one, the clones were turning into smoke in the air and returning to Han Sooyoung.
She was probably retrieving the proficiency they'd accumulated.
Han Sooyoung exclaimed,
“Oh! There's something I didn't tell you. I just remembered. Constellations came to visit while you were lying there dead.”
Don't give memories that important to your clones.
“I forgot their names, but they belonged to nebulae. <Vedas> and······ was it <Tamna>?”
Those were dangerous names.
Whether she knew how I felt or not, Han Sooyoung murmured languidly,
“They said some pretty vague stuff. Something about making the right choice······.”
“Couldn't you try remembering properly?”
“Sorry. Maybe I'll remember once I retrieve all my avatars······ Oh, and some weird guy who looked like a Goryeo warrior came, too.”
“A Goryeo warrior?”
“That one didn't really say anything and just left. Looked at your dead body for a bit, then went straight away.”
If it was a Goryeo warrior, there seemed to be a good chance it was Cheok Jungyeong.
<Olympus>, <Vedas>, and <Tamna>.
And even Cheok Jungyeong himself was taking action. It certainly seemed that something ominous was about to happen.
But just then, a sense that something didn't add up crossed my mind.
“Wait, the constellations came ‘in person’? Not their ‘incarnations’?”
“Yeah. They came in symbolic bodies. Why?”
“······Don't you see the problem?”
“Huh?”
“Even in symbolic bodies, there's no way constellations would spend that much probability to appear in a scenario area.”
Constellations, who feared probability more than anyone else in the world, would never descend in their symbolic bodies and appear in person.
Slowly looking around, I said,
“······I think I know where we are.”
As I'd suspected, we were inside a barrier.
But it wasn't an ordinary barrier.
A barrier so dreamlike that even constellations could visit in their symbolic bodies.
Han Sooyoung, who had belatedly realized something, spoke as well.
“······Mechanical Gateway Array.”
Mechanical Gateway Array (機門陳法). This was a technique favored by constellations who had mastered the principles of the Five Elements (五行), the Four Images (四象), and the Three Powers (三才).
But few beings could easily use a Mechanical Gateway Array on this scale. Only someone on the level of China's Crouching Dragon (臥龍) could wield such a technique at will.
But this was the Korean Peninsula. In that case······.
“Why don't you come out now?”
I spoke as I looked up into the air.
Aside from the Crouching Dragon, there was only one constellation who could freely control a Mechanical Gateway Array this large. And I'd already met that constellation.
“······It seems deceiving a constellation was too much to ask, after all.”
As the voice rang out, clouds gathered in the air and soon took the shape of a person.
It was a woman in her mid-to-late thirties, wearing a prison uniform.
“We've met before, haven't we?”
“This isn't a particularly welcome reunion.”
[The constellation, ‘First Spiritualist of Joseon,’ snickers at you.]
The incarnation of the First Spiritualist of Joseon—the constellation Jeon Woochi.
She was the foremost agent of the ‘King of Wanderers.’
“The king is waiting for you.”
Somehow, I felt I knew who had killed me.
It seemed things were taking the worst possible turn.
In any case, I had no other choice right now.
I nodded and said,
“Lead the way.”
“That bastard Kim Dokja······ He forgot me again.”
A small fortress stood proudly on a desolate plain. In truth, closer in size to a small country house, but still a defensive tower with more than enough armaments to deserve the name [Fortress].
Needless to say, it was Gong Pildu's [Armed Fortress].
Ratatatatat!

Gong Pildu unleashed shells at the monsters approaching the fortress. In the few weeks since he had entered the Dark Castle, he had been clinging to life in this hellish monster-infested area. Monsters swarming him at all hours. If it hadn't been for the coins Kim Dokja had given him before, his magic power would have run dry and he would have withered away and died long ago.
[The constellation, ‘Defense Master,’ is excited by the defense game.]
If only he hadn't had this perverse constellation as his sponsor, things wouldn't have gone this far.
“Fuuuuuck!”
His indiscriminate slaughter of the monsters had sharply raised his Dark Castle ranking, but the problem was that both his mental endurance and his magic power had now reached their limits.
“Is this as far as I go······?”
Watching the Armed Fortress's outer walls crumble beneath the monsters' claws, Gong Pildu looked defeated.
Then a golden slash flew in from the distance.
Rrrrrumble!
A powerful storm of ether splitting the entire plain. He opened his eyes wide, wondering if it could be Kim Dokja, but the man standing there was someone he hadn't expected.
“······Yoo Joonghyuk?”

A huge dragon flying through the storm. People Gong Pildu knew were riding on its back. Strength drained from Gong Pildu's body, and the fortress collapsed. Yoo Joonghyuk rushed over like a flash of light and hauled the falling Gong Pildu onto his back.
‘I've overused the power of a transcendent. I need to conserve my strength for a while.’
As he thought, Yoo Joonghyuk rotated his right arm, which had unleashed the golden slash.
The back of the hand that had gripped his sword was red and swollen.
Bzzzzt.

Even though it did not draw on a sponsor, a transcendent's power was still affected by probability. Things would improve as those restrictions were gradually lifted, but the probability permitted in scenario 9 was insufficient to make full use of a transcendent's power.
‘That takes care of retrieving Gong Pildu, too. Lee Seolhwa should be steadily raising her ranking on the western plain······.’
A plan progressing steadily.
Things were going more smoothly than in any scenario before.
‘Is Kim Dokja the only one left now?’
With that thought, Yoo Joonghyuk looked toward the northern plain.
‘The fate of the <Star Stream> isn't that easy to evade. What are you going to do, Kim Dokja?’
“Don't worry. There's a way out.”
“······That woman isn't the only problem. There's a whole bunch of tough bastards here. And they can even use a Mechanical Gateway Array. How are you going to fight them?”
“Just because it's a Mechanical Gateway Array doesn't mean there's no way to break it.”

Han Sooyoung and I were walking through the Mechanical Gateway Array, following Jeon Woochi's incarnation, Cho Youngran. Judging by the way she floated along instead of walking, she certainly did seem to be Jeon Woochi's incarnation.
Jeon Woochi. Along with Hong Gildong, a constellation whose power placed him among the very best of Korea's Historical-grade constellations······.
Han Sooyoung, who had been watching cautiously, spoke to me again.
“But didn't the reincarnator kill the King of Wanderers?”
“That's not someone who would die so easily.”
“······Come to think of it, you said you knew that king. Be specific. What the hell is your relationship?”
I let out a small sigh at her tone, as though she were grilling me.
“The most complicated relationship in the world.”
“Sounds kind of messy. An ex-girlfriend?”
“My mother.”
“What? Seriously? Uh······ Sorry.”
Han Sooyoung stammered, unusually flustered.
Perhaps she'd heard our conversation, because Cho Youngran turned around, her expression hardening.
“Step exactly where I step. If you step anywhere else, you'll immediately lose your way.”
I'd suspected it would be that kind of array.
As with all Mechanical Gateway Arrays, you would immediately lose your way in this one unless you advanced through the correct Gates of Life. I asked in a slightly dissatisfied tone,
“Can't you just deactivate the array before we go?”
“That would be difficult. We don't know what you might do.”
“That's funny. You're the ones who killed me, yet you're the ones who are afraid.”
“We know you have a resurrection ability.”
“Does that make it all right to kill me without warning?”
“I'm sorry about that. And we weren't trying to kill you. The attack was directed at that woman, but she used you as a shield.”
When I turned, Han Sooyoung was whistling and pretending not to notice.
Looking at Han Sooyoung's silly grin, I considered smacking her upside the head, but held back. I could question her about that later.
Seriously, if I hadn't had eight lives······ No, was it six now?
I turned toward Cho Youngran and asked,
“Why are you helping my mother?”
Cho Youngran hesitated briefly at my sudden question.

“Honestly, I don't understand why an incarnation of your caliber would follow someone else. With a constellation on the level of the ‘First Spiritualist of Joseon,’ you could aim for the king's position right now, depending on which stigmas you inherit.”
“······How did you know my constellation's identity?”
“It's obvious if we're talking about a constellation in Korea who has a Mechanical Gateway Array.”
Jeon Woochi wasn't Narrative-grade, but he had many advantages in the early scenarios, since manifesting his power cost relatively little probability.
Moreover, the fame and Stories he had accumulated were overwhelming compared with other constellations of the same grade, so he could rise to Narrative-grade as the scenarios progressed.
For similar reasons, Yoo Joonghyuk had often recruited Jeon Woochi as a companion to clear the early scenarios.
Cho Youngran answered,
“I'm not cut out to be a king.”
“Does my mother have something on you?”
Cho Youngran started to say something, then closed her mouth again.
“Tell me honestly. I might be able to help.”
“She's deceiving you.”
Jeon Woochi would be a major asset if I could get him on my side.
Of course, I wasn't getting my hopes up.
“She saved my daughter.”
Just as I'd thought.
“I see. Repaying her for saving a life······ After something like that, I suppose you'd have reason to be loyal.”
Cho Youngran's eyebrow twitched at my words.
“You're being sarcastic?”
“Yes. Because I think that ‘rescue’ was very calculated.”
“······Calculated?”
“Don't you think there's something strange about my mother?”
“In what way?”
“Like how she adapts a little too well to this world, or knows all sorts of information that shouldn't be available at this point.”
For a moment, Han Sooyoung looked at me in disbelief. Cho Youngran answered,
“······What are you trying to say?”
“How about I put it this way? My mother knew which constellation you would get.”
“She probably saved your daughter with the intention of using you from the beginning. That's the kind of person she is.”
Cho Youngran······ My memory wasn't exact, but I thought a woman with a name like that had once become Jeon Woochi's incarnation.
A character who lost her daughter, became Jeon Woochi's incarnation, and resolved to take revenge on the world.
I didn't know when I'd told my mother that story, but if she'd listened and remembered that information, it wasn't far-fetched to think she'd planned to use this woman.
But Cho Youngran said something unexpected.
“You misunderstand her.”
“Misunderstand?”
Cho Youngran's gaze as she stared at me.
It was the kind of look I hated most, tinged with unwelcome pity.
“Sookyung-ssi isn't the bad person you think she is.”
Was it because an unwarranted sense of defiance surged through me?
I answered curtly.
“No one knows her better than I do.”
“Children are usually the ones who understand their parents' hearts the least. And we're here.”
When I looked ahead, something like a front door had appeared.
Cho Youngran said to Han Sooyoung,
“You can't go in. Stay with me.”
“Tch, your mother must be awfully shy around strangers. Have a good visit.”
I nodded and placed my hand on the front door.
Behind this door was probably the most formidable enemy of this scenario.
Cho Youngran said,
“Just ring the bell there.”
Ding-dong.
Somehow, the old-fashioned chime stirred a familiar memory.
It sounded like a doorbell I'd heard a very long time ago.
My mother's voice came from inside.
“Come in.”

When I opened the door and stepped inside, I found the familiar entrance to a family home. Several pairs of shoes were neatly arranged. Among them were small shoes that seemed to belong to a child. The sense of déjà vu grows stronger. The familiar furnishings of the house. Modest decorations, neither too lavish nor too antique, yet clearly not chosen by someone without a sense of style.

As I enter the living room, a familiar space appears. The wall clock and television I'd forgotten. A sofa whose texture I feel I would know without even sitting on it. Even the table's position was familiar.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ trembles.]
Really······ This was a truly twisted idea of fun.
My mother sat on the living room sofa in an elegant outfit.
“That took a while. How does it feel to be home after so long?”
“I'd have been better off staying dead.”
“I'm glad you look healthy.”
“Thanks to a certain someone, I only just came back from the dead.”
My mother had probably chosen this place to gain the upper hand.
The conversation we were about to have would probably be the decisive contest that determined the two remaining scenarios.
“I heard Nirvana killed you. How were you still alive?”
“Deceiving someone like that is nothing. Have you forgotten? I have plenty of information about the future, too.”
I'd expected as much. But to have fooled Nirvana······ Even though she was my mother, I couldn't quite gauge the extent of this person's abilities.
Perhaps the greatest threat to me right now wasn't Yoo Joonghyuk or the constellations, but this very person.
“So you were alive, but didn't even come to my funeral.”
“Why would I go to the funeral of an unfilial son who left his mother behind and died first?”
“And as if that wasn't enough, you had your subordinates kill me again.”

“I found that unfilial son's unfilial behavior so offensive that I killed him once more. Do you need another funeral this time? I see you've made a lot of good companions. They were all crying their eyes out, not even knowing you would come back to life······.”
The way she spoke confirmed that this person was indeed my mother.
I took a brief, deep breath.
I could never let my guard down while talking to my mother.
And the real conversation was probably about to begin.
“Why did you kill me?”
My mother gave a small laugh and answered,
“Incarnation Kim Dokja will die at the hands of the person he loves most.”
“······How did you find out about that, too?”
“Yoo Sangah-ssi told me. She begged me to save you.”
It seemed Yoo Sangah-ssi had come to see my mother.
“Come to think of it, you've come with a different young woman this time. Have your tastes changed already? Honestly, your mom likes Yoo Sangah-ssi better.”
“Stop meddling in things that don't concern you. Besides, that makes even less sense. Why did you kill me when she asked you to save me?”
“In any case, it seems the prophecy was fulfilled thanks to me. Wasn't it?”
“What?”
Suddenly, my thoughts become tangled.
No, so right now······.
My mother smiled and said,
“The prophecy said it, didn't it? ‘The person you love most.’ That's why I killed you.”
It was laughable to hear the person I hated more than anyone say such a thing.

And yet, the moment I heard it, a feeling I couldn't quite describe unsettled me. I definitely hated my mother. Because of her, my life had been ruined, turned into a mess. And yet······ this complicated feeling.
“I see. You thought that killing me would make you the person I loved most? Because fate said so?”
“Isn't that a development that often appears in those novels you like?”
“Then you've failed completely.”
Fate had clearly said I would be killed by ‘someone I loved.’
In that case, my last death should have fulfilled my fate.
“The fate messages are still appearing.”
It was true.
For a little while now, those tiresome messages had been sounding in my ears again.
[A great fate desires your certain death.]
It had even added a qualifier.
‘Certain death.’
What ‘King Oedipus’ had said when he appeared in my dream was right.
This Story. It meant I couldn't evade it with ‘Eight Lives.’
“At the very least, that means you're not someone I love.”
At my words, my mother fell silent for a moment.
That silence made me feel a little elated.
The fact that this ‘mother’ had hoped I loved her, and the thought that I could hurt those feelings, elated me.
But when my mother spoke next, her tone suggested she'd expected this.
“Hmm, so it is as I thought.”
“I still wanted to try it. It might have brought your fate to an end. You had plenty of lives left anyway.”
“Don't talk as though you did it for me.”
“I love you.”
Her words sent a shiver through my entire body.
Why was she suddenly saying that now, after all this time?
“What do you mean?”
“I'm your mom, aren't I?”
A corner of my heart began to ache as I watched my mother smile.
Did she really believe she could say something like that and have it accepted?
Did she believe those few words could negate the ten-odd years I'd spent struggling alone in pain because of her?
I glared silently at my mother.
My mother, loves, me.
I couldn't bring myself to use [Lie Detection].
Sometimes, there are words like that in this world.
Words that hurt too much, whether they are true or false.
I spoke as though sighing.
“It's too late.”
“I know.”
“Then why······?”
“I wanted to say it at least once. I don't think I've ever said it to you.”
For a while, we said nothing, measuring out the silence. Only the quiet ticking of the wall clock told us that this moment was passing. Like the turning of a page with nothing written on it.
I opened my mouth like a writer barely managing to squeeze out a first sentence.
“······What was life in prison like?”
“You came to see me often. Even without my saying······.”
“You never told me anything.”
“Why didn't you say anything? I went to see you so many times······.”
I hadn't hated my mother from the beginning.
Even when she killed my father.
Even when she went to prison for it.
Even when relatives descended on us, stripped away our family's assets, and dumped me in a relative's home like leftover clearance merchandise.
I hadn't hated or resented my mother.
“How can a person be so shameless?”
The reason I came to resent my mother was simple.
“Why on earth did you say nothing to me? And why······ did you write that story?”
Someone might say this.
That she'd sold the book and must have become rich from the royalties in the end, so wasn't that a good thing?
I didn't really know whether the royalties Mom received helped support me. My relatives had always treated me as though I didn't exist.

“It was so hard for me. Whether I went to school, walked down the street, or met someone, it felt like the whole world was talking about me. Moving house or changing schools made no difference. I was always ‘the murderer's son.’”
People who have never experienced it don't know.
How relentless this world can be.
The feeling of reporters lurking outside my home, of every gaze in the world following me.
“Even so, perhaps I could have endured that much.”
If my mother had said even a single word to me, perhaps I would have been all right.
If she'd told me to hold on a little longer, that I could endure it.
Even if she'd sold my story for money, if she'd only let me know she was on my side.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ trembles violently.]
[The stigma, ‘Self-Justification Lv.2,’ activates!]
I looked at my mother.
I hadn't misunderstood anything.
My mother had made a lot of money by selling my life and her own.
That same mother opened her mouth.

Only when I looked down did I realize what condition I was in.
Below my knees, my legs were gone.
Legs that had vanished cleanly, as though crushed in a press. Blood flowed ceaselessly from the severed ends. A tentacle had probably crushed them while I was using the Three Sword Style.
Damn it.
For this to happen when I was almost there.
In the distance, I could see the god's wound gradually repairing itself.
Without my knees, there was no way I could leap that distance.
“Kim Dokja.”
I turned my head, and there was Yoo Joonghyuk, covered in blood.
Staggering over, Yoo Joonghyuk silently took hold of my collar and hauled me up, then slung me over his shoulder.
Looking at the god's wound, Yoo Joonghyuk asked.
“I just need to throw you in there, right?”
“······Can you do it?”
Yoo Joonghyuk didn't answer.
He simply showed everything through his actions.
Yoo Joonghyuk climbed through the air as though it were a staircase.

Stepping on the incoming tentacles, and sometimes on his own magic field with [Air Steps]. I began to hear creaking sounds from his body too. His body had already reached its limit. But Yoo Joonghyuk showed no sign of giving up.
Climbing, and climbing again.
Before long, the wind far above the ground washed over my cheeks.
Yoo Joonghyuk stepped onto a magic field in the air and stopped.
When I lifted my head and looked ahead, I saw the god's wound.
But despite having no time, Yoo Joonghyuk hesitated.
He hesitated, gripping my collar tightly.
“······I won't have to hold another funeral, will I?”
The question was so unlike Yoo Joonghyuk that I couldn't help chuckling.
“Even if I die, I'll come back to life, you idiot.”
“That isn't what I mean.”
Yoo Joonghyuk's expression was serious.
The wind at that height sliced sharply between Yoo Joonghyuk and me.
I looked at him for a moment, then asked.
“Remember the second scenario?”
The subway at Oksu Station.
The sight of Yoo Joonghyuk appearing as he smashed everything in his way.
A cold-blooded regressor who would use any means necessary to achieve his ends.
That once-calm gaze of Yoo Joonghyuk's was wavering.
Who could have known back then.
That he and I would become companions.
I hadn't wanted to admit it all this time, but now I had to.
What had seemed utterly impossible had become reality, and
I really was making my way through the scenarios with him.
So now, I could say it.
Just as I had when I first met him.
With a grin, in the way that suited us best.
“Let go of me already and fuck off, you goddamn bastard.”
